groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: A person may not practice or offer to practice the profession of architecture, engineering, land surveying, or landscape architecture in the state, or use in connection with the person's name or other

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.value: State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors
example.quote: There is created the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors. The board shall administer the provisions of this chapter

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.value: State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors
example.quote: There is created the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors.

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.quote: The board consists of two civil engineers, two land surveyors, one mining engineer, one electrical or mechanical engineer, one engineer from another branch of the profession of engineering, two archit

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.

example.quote: To be qualified for admission to an examination to practice architecture in the State of Arkansas, an applicant shall be at least twenty-one (21) years of age.

fields.meaning: Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.

example.quote: An applicant for registration as an architect, engineer, land surveyor, or landscape architect must be of good character and reputation

fields.meaning: Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.

example.value: Evidence satisfactory to the board of the applicant's education, training, and experience
example.quote: shall submit evidence satisfactory to the board of the applicant's education, training, and experience
school or college of architecture accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB)

fields.meaning: The comparable education FLOOR as a normalized rung. Populate whenever licensure is gated on a degree; null only if the statute is silent on education.

example.quote: Graduation after a course of study of a length as the board by rule shall determine from a school or college of architecture accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB)

fields.meaning: How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

example.quote: shall submit evidence satisfactory to the board of the applicant's education, training, and experience

fields.meaning: True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

example.quote: The procedure and standards shall at least meet the requirements adopted by recognized national examining councils for these professions.

fields.meaning: Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

example.value: bachelor's or higher degree with 3 years experience

fields.meaning:
Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

example.quote: shall submit evidence satisfactory to the board of the applicant's education, training, and experience

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

example.quote: shall submit evidence satisfactory to the board of the applicant's education, training, and experience

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)

example.value: as the board by rule shall deem appropriate
example.quote: An additional period of practical experience in architectural work under the responsible control of a registered architect or architects as the board by rule shall deem appropriate.

fields.meaning: e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'

example.value: practical experience in architectural work under the responsible control of a registered architect
example.quote: practical experience in architectural work under the responsible control of a registered architect or architects

fields.meaning: Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: Examinations shall be held at least once each year; standards must at least meet requirements adopted by recognized national examining councils.

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.

example.value: state (administered per board regulations, meeting national examining council standards)

fields.meaning: Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.

example.quote: pay biennially to the secretary of said board during the month of November, a fee not to exceed Four Hundred Dollars ($400.00)

fields.meaning: Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

example.quote: establishing continuing education requirements for registrants that must be completed before a certificate may be renewed; the requirements may not exceed standards established by a national accrediti
Five hours of coursework regarding disability access requirements... Five hours of coursework regarding zero net carbon design for all renewals occurring on or after January 1, 2023.
All licenses issued or renewed under this chapter shall expire two years from the last day of the month in which the license was issued

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']

value: technical and professional subjects appropriate to professional architectural practice
example.quote: all registered architects remain informed of those technical and professional subjects that the board deems appropriate to professional architectural practice

fields.meaning: Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: A person holding a certificate of registration authorizing the person to practice architecture in a state, territory, or possession of the United States, the District of Columbia, or a foreign country

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Must hold a certificate of registration from another U.S. state, territory, D.C., or foreign country (or an NCARB certificate), issued under requirements comparable to Alaska's requirements.
example.quote: may, upon application, be registered in accordance with the regulations of the board if the person's certificate was issued under requirements comparable to the requirements in this state

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: There is created the State Board of Registration for Architects, Engineers, and Land Surveyors. The board shall administer the provisions of this chapter

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.

example.quote: "Board" means the Illinois Architecture Licensing Board appointed by the Secretary.

fields.meaning: Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

example.quote: 7 members who shall serve in an advisory capacity to the Secretary

fields.meaning: Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

example.value: National Council of Architectural Registration Boards (NCARB)
example.quote: holding a certificate of qualification issued by the National Council of Architectural Registration Boards, may, upon application, be registered in accordance with the regulations of the board

fields.meaning: Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

example.quote: school or college of architecture accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB)

fields.meaning: Which UORF model the state applies to this profession (license / mandatory_cert / registration / etc).

example.quote: A person may not practice or offer to practice the profession of architecture, engineering, land surveying, or landscape architecture in the state, or use in connection with the person's name or other

fields.meaning: What SHAPE of credential does the state issue, independent of whether holding it is mandatory? license / certification / registration / exemption / none. Pairs with is_mandatory to decompose the legacy regulatory_model rung.

example.quote: An applicant who fulfills the requirements set out by the board shall be awarded a certificate of registration authorizing the holder to offer or perform services or work for the public, or to certify

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

example.quote: A person may not practice or offer to practice the profession of architecture, engineering, land surveying, or landscape architecture in the state, or use in connection with the person's name or other

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

example.quote: use in connection with the person's name or otherwise assume or advertise a title or description tending to convey the impression that the person is an architect, an engineer, a land surveyor, or a la

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict practice of the profession's scope to licensees? True if performing the scope without a license is prohibited (independent of title use).

example.quote: A person may not practice or offer to practice the profession of architecture, engineering, land surveying, or landscape architecture in the state

fields.meaning: Grounds on which the board may discipline a licensee. Typical statutes list 5-15.
snake_case key, e.g. 'fraud_in_obtaining_license'
One-line plain-English description

example.value: Fraud or deceit in obtaining a certificate of registration

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to carry insurance (e.g., professional liability, surety insurance)?

example.quote: an architectural corporation shall provide adequate security by insurance or otherwise for claims against it by its clients arising out of the rendering of professional services.

fields.meaning: Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?

example.quote: Any business, including, but not limited to, a Professional Service Corporation, that includes the practice of architecture within its stated purposes, practices architecture, or holds itself out as a

fields.meaning: Statutory citations supporting the licensure fields above.

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.value: professional service or creative work in the design of buildings, the teaching of advanced architectural courses in institutions of higher learning, consultation, investigation, evaluation, planning, design, and professional observation of construction of public or private buildings, works, or projects, and architectural review of drawings and specifications by regulatory agencies
example.quote: "practice of architecture" means professional service or creative work in the design of buildings, the teaching of advanced architectural courses in institutions of higher learning, consultation, inve

value: consultation
investigation
evaluation
planning
design
professional observation of construction
architectural review of drawings and specifications
mechanical, electrical, or structural design of minor importance (by regulation)

fields.meaning: Whether/how the profession may prescribe, administer, or dispense drugs.
Statutory citations supporting the scope fields above.

groups.intro: Fields discovered specifically for this profession (auto-derived from its statutes); they vary profession to profession.

fields.meaning: Whether the state offers a separate certification credential for interior designers alongside the architect license.

example.quote: A person seeking to obtain a certificate of registration as a registered interior designer and a seal pursuant to s. 481.221 must provide the department with his or her name and address and written pr

fields.meaning: Whether the statute separately defines 'interior design services' as a distinct regulated activity from the practice of architecture.

example.quote: "interior designer" means a person who: Engages in: Consultation, study, design analysis, drawing, space planning, and specification for nonstructural or nonseismic interior construction with due conc

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly authorizes and regulates design-build project delivery by architectural firms or entities.

example.quote: a general contractor who is certified or registered pursuant to the provisions of chapter 489 is not required to be licensed as an architect when negotiating or performing services under a design-buil

fields.meaning: The legal business entity forms in which architects are permitted to practice.

value: Corporation
Limited Liability Company
Limited Liability Partnership
Limited Partnership
Partnership (all-registrant)
example.quote: This chapter does not prevent a corporation, limited liability company, limited liability partnership, or limited partnership from offering architectural, engineering, land surveying, or landscape arc

fields.meaning: The minimum fraction of ownership, directors, or partners in an architectural firm that must be licensed architects (as opposed to other licensed design professionals).

example.value: at least one must be an architect registered in Alabama; the overall minimum two-thirds must be architects or professional engineers registered under the laws of any United States jurisdiction
example.quote: A minimum of two-thirds of those responsible for controlling the activities of the entity, including officers, partners, directors, members, and others depending on the legal structure of the entity,

fields.meaning: The minimum fraction of ownership, directors, or partners in an architectural firm that must be licensed in architecture, engineering, or landscape architecture combined.

example.quote: A minimum of two-thirds of those responsible for controlling the activities of the entity, including officers, partners, directors, members, and others depending on the legal structure of the entity,

fields.meaning: Whether a licensed architect is required to obtain and affix an official seal to drawings, specifications, and other design documents.

example.quote: When a registrant issues final drawings, specifications, surveys, plats, plates, reports, or similar documents, the registrant shall stamp the documents with the seal and sign the seal.

fields.meaning: Whether an architect must surrender their seal or stamp to the board upon forfeiture, revocation, suspension, expiration, or death.

example.quote: It shall be unlawful for anyone to stamp or seal any document with the seal after the certificate or the registrant named thereon has expired or been suspended or revoked.

fields.meaning: Specific subject-area requirements mandated for continuing education credit toward license renewal.

value: technical and professional subjects appropriate to professional architectural practice
example.quote: all registered architects remain informed of those technical and professional subjects that the board deems appropriate to professional architectural practice

fields.meaning: Topics explicitly prohibited from counting toward continuing education requirements.

value: repetition of the same course within a single renewal cycle
example.quote: An applicant may not repeat for credit the same continuing education course, program or activity within a license renewal cycle.

fields.meaning: Circumstances under which the board may waive all or part of the continuing education requirement.

value: Active duty military service
example.quote: a board may establish and implement a waiver of continuing education requirements for renewal of a license regulated by the board for the period in which a licensee is engaged in active duty military

fields.meaning: Categories of structures or projects explicitly exempt from the architect licensure requirement.

value: single-family residence for own use and occupancy and related site work
farm or ranch buildings and their grounds unless the public health, safety, or welfare is involved
building used only as a residence by not more than four families and not more than two stories high
building used only as a residence by not more than two families and not more than three stories high in a municipality with an applicable building or residential code
garage, workshop, or similar building containing less than 2,000 square feet for private noncommercial use
alterations or repairs not changing or affecting structural system or safety and not affecting public health, safety, or welfare
federal government buildings designed by officer or employee in official capacity
work designed by a professional architect, engineer, or landscape architect (contractor performing or supervising)
example.quote: a person preparing drawings or specifications for (A) a building for the person's own use and occupancy as a single family residence and related site work for that building; (B) farm or ranch building

fields.meaning: Whether possession of an NCARB certificate constitutes prima facie evidence of meeting the state's licensure qualifications for reciprocity purposes.

example.quote: the applicant may demonstrate appropriate qualifications by a combination of education, experience, and examination endorsed by NCARB and approved by the board.

fields.meaning: The criminal classification and maximum penalty for a first offense of unauthorized practice of architecture.

example.value: Misdemeanor; fine not more than $10,000, or imprisonment for not more than one year, or both
example.quote: is guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction is punishable by a fine of not more than $10,000, or by imprisonment for not more than one year, or by both

fields.meaning: The criminal classification and penalty range for a second or subsequent offense of unauthorized practice of architecture.

example.value: In connection with natural disaster repair, punishable by a fine up to $10,000, or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code for 16 months, 2 or 3 years, or both; or a fine up to $1,000 or county jail not exceeding one year, or both.
example.quote: shall be punished by a fine up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code for 16 months, or for two or three years, or by both

fields.meaning: Maximum civil penalty in dollars the board may levy on a current licensee or unauthorized practitioner for violations.

example.quote: A civil penalty levied under this section may not exceed $5,000 for each offense.
